description: Describe the normal curve N(μ, σ²) and use the 68–95–99.7% rule for quick estimates.
mastery_criteria: Reads μ and σ from N(μ, σ²)

name: Normal probabilities and quantiles
chapter: Methods U4 · T3 Continuous random variables and the normal distribution
description: Use technology to calculate normal probabilities and the value with a given probability below it.
mastery_criteria: Calculates P(a < X < b) with technology
Standardises to compare with the standard normal

name: Random sampling and bias
chapter: Methods U4 · T4 Sampling and proportions
description: Describe random samples, sources of bias, and procedures that make a sample random.
mastery_criteria: Explains why larger samples vary less

name: The sample proportion
chapter: Methods U4 · T4 Sampling and proportions
description: Treat the sample proportion p̂ as a random variable with mean p and standard deviation √(p(1 − p)/n).
mastery_criteria: Calculates the mean and standard deviation of p̂
Explains how n affects the spread

name: Approximate normality of the sample proportion
chapter: Methods U4 · T4 Sampling and proportions
description: Use the approximately normal distribution of p̂ for large samples to estimate probabilities.
mastery_criteria: Knows when the normal approximation is reasonable

name: Confidence intervals for a proportion
chapter: Methods U4 · T5 Interval estimates for proportions
description: Calculate an approximate confidence interval p̂ ± z√(p̂(1 − p̂)/n) for a population proportion.
mastery_criteria: Calculates p̂ and its standard error
Uses the right z for the confidence level

name: Margin of error, confidence level and sample size
chapter: Methods U4 · T5 Interval estimates for proportions
description: Relate the margin of error to the confidence level and sample size, and find the sample size needed for a given margin.
mastery_criteria: Explains the effect of confidence level and n

name: Interpreting confidence intervals
chapter: Methods U4 · T5 Interval estimates for proportions
description: Interpret confidence intervals correctly, including that they vary between samples and that most, but not all, contain p.
mastery_criteria: States the repeated-sampling meaning of 95% confidence
Uses an interval to judge a claim
Expects some intervals to miss p
